about: How desktop apps really work, for AI agents: which keys do what, and what to avoid. Shortcuts here are the apps' own defaults (Windows). 'canvas': the app draws its own interface, so accessibility trees see little — prefer the shortcuts.

apps.name: Windows
notes: File Explorer: type a path into the address bar (Ctrl+L) instead of clicking through folders.
To find a file, use the search box (Ctrl+E) rather than scrolling.
keys: snap the window to half the screen

apps.name: Web browser
notes: To go somewhere, put the address in the address bar (Ctrl+L, type, Enter) — no need to hunt for links.
To find words on a long page, use Find (Ctrl+F) instead of scrolling and squinting.

apps.name: Microsoft Word
notes: Format by selecting text then using the shortcut; don't hunt through the ribbon.

apps.name: Microsoft Excel
notes: Type into a cell, then Enter (down) or Tab (right). Formulas start with =.
Jump to a cell with the Name Box (Ctrl+G, type A1, Enter) instead of scrolling.
keys: jump to the edge of the data

apps.name: Visual Studio Code
notes: Open any file by name with Ctrl+P; run any command by name with Ctrl+Shift+P — faster and surer than clicking menus.

apps.name: FL Studio
notes: FL Studio draws its own interface: the Playlist, Channel Rack and Piano Roll are canvases, so screen controls can't see notes or clips. Use the window keys and tools below, and the menus by name.
Don't drag clips or notes pixel by pixel. Set the snap (magnet) first so placements land on the grid, select what you want, then use a tool or the quantize command.
To bring in a beat or melody you made elsewhere, drag the .mid file onto the Playlist or a channel — far more exact than drawing notes by hand.
keys: select all (in the window in front)

apps.name: Ableton Live
notes: Arrangement clips are on a canvas: put the playhead where you want, then split there rather than dragging edges.

apps.name: Adobe Premiere Pro
notes: Cut at the playhead (Ctrl+K) instead of aiming the razor; remove gaps with Ripple Delete instead of dragging clips together.

apps.name: CapCut
notes: Split at the playhead (Ctrl+B) instead of dragging clip edges.

apps.name: Adobe Photoshop
notes: Pick a tool by its key, work on its own layer (Ctrl+J or Ctrl+Shift+N), and use Free Transform (Ctrl+T) to resize or rotate exactly.

apps.name: Blender
notes: Keys act on what's under the mouse pointer: keep the pointer over the 3D view. Type exact numbers after G/R/S (e.g. S 2 Enter) instead of dragging.

apps.name: Figma
notes: Figma is a canvas: pick tools by key and type exact sizes in the right-hand panel rather than dragging.

apps.name: Discord
notes: Jump to any server, channel or person with the quick switcher (Ctrl+K) instead of scrolling the sidebar.

apps.name: School sites (Blackboard, Canvas, Moodle, Google Classroom)
notes: Answer each question, and on Blackboard press Save Answer when there is one.
Never press Submit / Turn in / Finish attempt yourself — stop and let the person review and submit.
Instructions, rubrics and due dates are often behind links (Syllabus, Assignment details): read them before answering.
